prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: מערכת שעות כיתת י'2 – סמסטר א' (language he, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 6 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "ראשון" spans 1 col × 2 row; "שני" spans 1 col × 2 row; "שלישי" spans 1 col × 3 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "יום" · longest unbreakable word 41px · one-line width 41px
  col 2: header "שעה" · longest unbreakable word 48px · one-line width 89px
  col 3: header "מקצוע" · longest unbreakable word 63px · one-line width 63px
  col 4: header "מורה" · longest unbreakable word 42px · one-line width 68px
  col 5: header "חדר" · longest unbreakable word 46px · one-line width 76px
  col 6: header "הערות" · longest unbreakable word 64px · one-line width 700px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A Hebrew RTL class timetable for grade י'2, semester א', used to find when a lesson occurs, who teaches it, where it meets, and any special instructions.","reading":"Readers scan from the right: first the merged day block, then the time, then subject/teacher/room as the lesson identity, and finally the notes as exceptions or instructions. Day rowspans group consecutive lessons, so those blocks must remain visually coherent.","groups":["יום + שעה — temporal anchors read first and define each rowspan block","מקצוע + מורה + חדר — the lesson's identity and location, compared across rows","הערות — secondary free-text annotations that can absorb wrapping"],"keep_intact":["time ranges such as 08:15–09:00","day labels ראשון, שני, שלישי","subject names","teacher names at least at word level","room numbers and room labels at word level"],"may_wrap":["הערות prose, which is long and naturally multi-line","multi-word room labels such as אולם ספורט at spaces","teacher full names at spaces only in a notes-priority design"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r2A: widths [62, 110, 84, 66, 97, 300] · table 720×500px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 60, 60, 83, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [62, 110, 84, 89, 70, 304] · table 720×500px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 60, 60, 83, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r2A","good":"The notes column at 300px (279px of content) keeps annotations to at most 3 lines, so row heights stay predictable. Room labels are intact on one line — \"אולם ספורט\" and \"מעבדה 1\" both read cleanly — and all six column headers sit on a single line, so the header band is calm and the day/time anchors line up neatly down the right edge.","problems":"The teacher column is the failure point: every single name breaks into two stacked fragments (רונית/לוי, אבי/שפירא, שרה/כהן, דוד/מזרחי, יעל/ברק, מיכל/אדרי, עומר/פרץ). Since מורה is part of the lesson's identity, the reader cannot compare teachers down the column at a glance; the eye keeps re-assembling two-line blobs. Meanwhile the room column, whose content is mostly a three-digit number, carries visible slack — so the allocation is inverted relative to information value: the column with the most semantic weight is starved while the sparsest numeric column is comfortable. The result is a grid where every lesson row looks vertically ragged in one column and airy in another.","cause":"מורה = 66px leaves only 45px of content against a 68px one-line width, so all names must wrap. חדר = 97px gives exactly the 76px needed for \"אולם ספורט\", which is why the room column is safe but the teacher column is not."},{"design":"r2B","good":"Teacher names now sit on one line (מורה = 89px gives the full 68px), so the lesson identity reads as a single unit and the column scans vertically. מקצוע, שעה and יום are unchanged and intact, headers are all single-line, and — importantly — total row heights are identical to r2A (max 3 lines), because the room wrap only happens in rows already made tall by their notes. So the fix cost nothing in table height.","problems":"The room column is now the cramped one: \"אולם ספורט\" splits into אולם / ספורט and \"מעבדה 1\" into מעבדה / 1, while bare numbers like 204, 112, 305 sit alone on a line. The room column therefore looks inconsistent — sometimes one line, sometimes two — and in the last row the two-line room label looks stranded beside a three-line note. The subject column is also at exactly zero slack, which is risky.","cause":"חדר = 70px leaves 49px of content, well under the 76px one-line width of \"אולם ספורט\", so that cell must wrap; מקצוע = 84px gives exactly the 63px of \"מתמטיקה\" with no safety margin."}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"single-line-strict","widths":[62,110,84,89,97,277],"change":"Spend everything on making every non-notes column single-line: day 62, time 110, subject 84, teacher 89, room 97 (the 76px \"אולם ספורט\" fits), and give the remainder — 277px — to הערות. Now the only column that wraps is the notes, which is prose and should wrap. Cost: notes content drops from 279px to 256px, so the longest annotations may grow from 3 to 4 lines and those rows get taller; the grid becomes calmer even though the table gets a little longer."},{"name":"notes-first","widths":[62,110,86,89,72,300],"change":"Refines r2B: keep the proven 300px notes column (known 3-line maximum, so row heights stay as rendered), keep teacher at 89 so names stay whole, add 2px slack to מקצוע (86 → 65px content, so מתמטיקה cannot break), and take those 2px back from חדר (72). Room labels wrap only in the two rows that are already tall because of their notes, so the wrap is visually free; this is the safe, no-regression option."},{"name":"room-wraps-once","widths":[62,110,84,89,84,290],"change":"A middle trade-off between the two extremes: room at 84px (63px content) is enough for \"מעבדה 1\" and all numeric rooms on one line, and only \"אולם ספורט\" — in the last row, which is already three lines tall from its note — splits at its space. That buys 290px for הערות (269px content), comfortably above the width where the current notes reach three lines, so the annotation column stays wide while the room column looks consistent in six of seven rows."}]}
